name: Python
summary: The recommended language for data, automation and AI — from the first line to the type hints, the tests and the tooling a team will expect of you.
prerequisites: No previous programming required: Python is taught here from the first line.
syllabus: Object orientation, modules and the standard library
What separates a script from Python: decorators, generators and context managers
Type hints, and the checker that reads them
Tests with pytest, and code a tool formats for you
Files, JSON, CSV and regular expressions
Virtual environments, packages, and the essential libraries
topics: Installation, the interpreter and your first script
Types, variables, operators and string formatting
Collections: lists, tuples, dictionaries and sets
Conditionals, loops and comprehensions (list/dict comprehensions)
Functions: arguments, return values, scope and lambdas
Object orientation: classes, inheritance and special methods
Modules, packages and the standard library
Errors and exceptions: try, except, else and finally
Files, JSON and CSV
Regular expressions: matching, groups and substitution
Iterators and generators: producing one value at a time
Decorators: the function that wraps another function
Context managers, and writing a `with` block of your own
Type hints: annotating arguments, returns and collections
mypy and pyright: the checker that reads the annotations
Testing with pytest: assertions, fixtures, parametrisation and coverage
Formatting and linting with black and ruff
Virtual environments (venv), pip and requirements
uv, Poetry and pyproject.toml: how a project declares itself today
Data structures and a sense of complexity (Big-O)
pandas for tables and requests for consuming APIs
